recent.question: Saudi Oil Pipeline (East-West) restarts by October 31?
recent.what_happened: On October 6, 2026, the same day as the forecast, Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman publicly said the East-West pipeline was pumping 5.8 million b/d. A government official saying the pipeline is currently operating meets the rules, so the market resolved Yes.
recent.what_we_missed: Several independent sources already showed the pipeline running at about 80% of capacity, and the ministry had publicly confirmed a restoration in April. A government statement was therefore likely to follow soon. The forecaster treated the ministry's silence so far as if it would continue, and went to 14% against a market price of 41%.
recent.lesson: If the physical event has clearly already happened and the only question is whether officials will announce it, expect an official statement within a few weeks, especially when the same government has announced similar restorations before. Don't bet heavily on continued silence.

suggested_change.change: Flag any forecast more than 20 points below the market on a question that depends on an announcement when the underlying event has already been reported as happening, and require an explicit reason why officials would stay silent until the deadline.

recent.question: Will Bitcoin dip to $80,000 in October?
recent.what_happened: On Oct 11, BTC was around $83,000, only about 3.6% above the $80,000 strike, and it had already hit about $80,365 on Oct 8. Around Oct 26, ahead of the Oct 27–28 FOMC meeting and amid ETF outflows, BTC dropped below $80,000. Reports put the intraday low under $79,300, so the market resolved YES.
recent.what_we_missed: The facts we gave the forecaster measured everything against a $70,000 strike ("15.6% above the $70,000 strike", "no report shows trading near $70,000"), but this question's strike is $80,000. That made the gap look about four times bigger than it was. With a 3–4% gap, 20 days left, a near-touch three days earlier, and an FOMC meeting inside the window, the chance of touching $80,000 should have been roughly 65–75%, not 41–44%. The market's price of 56.5% was closer.
recent.lesson: Before using a fact sheet, check that its strike matches the question title, and work out the distance to the strike yourself from the current price.

suggested_change.change: Add an automatic check that pulls the strike from the question title and resolution rules, and flags any research fact that cites a different strike before the forecast goes out.

recent.question: Will Bitcoin dip to $77,500 in October?
recent.what_happened: BTC drifted down through late October. A hawkish macro backdrop (oil above $117, risk-off selling in tech stocks and gold) combined with weak sentiment after a large crypto hack. Around the Oct 28 FOMC and into Oct 31, BTC traded near $77,000–77,150, which crossed the $77,500 strike on Binance.
recent.what_we_missed: Little could have been known on Oct 10. The forecast already sat above the market (0.44 vs 0.365), and it correctly weighted September's repeated trades below $77.5k, the FOMC and macro events still to come, and the 50-week MA support near $77k. A 6.2% drop over about three weeks, with recent weekly ranges of 5–17%, was close to a coin flip.
recent.lesson: For monthly crypto 'dip to X' markets where the strike is about 6% away, more than three weeks remain, and the asset traded below the strike in recent weeks, touch probabilities near or slightly above 50% are reasonable, so don't anchor on the lower market price.

suggested_change.change: Keep using volatility-based touch probability estimates. This forecast was well calibrated and leaned the right way relative to the market.

recent.question: Will Bitcoin dip to $82,500 in October?
recent.what_happened: On Oct 7, ahead of the FOMC minutes, Bitcoin fell from above $87,000 to near $83,000 as more than $600M in leveraged longs were liquidated. It kept falling on Oct 8, and StatMuse data puts that day's low near $80,337, well under the $82,500 strike. This happened within hours of the judgment time, so the market resolved YES early.
recent.what_we_missed: The forecaster's 'current' price of about $85,500–$85,900 was hours out of date. By 00:35 UTC Oct 8, BTC was already trading near $83,000, roughly 0.6% above the strike. The market's 0.89 price reflected this, and we ignored that large gap without checking a live quote.
recent.lesson: For barrier-touch markets, get a live exchange quote from the moment of judgment. If the market price is far from your estimate, assume the price has just moved until you can show otherwise.

suggested_change.change: For crypto price-threshold markets, require a timestamped Binance spot quote taken within 15 minutes of judgment, and block any forecast more than 30 points from the market price until a fresh live price confirms it.

recent.question: Will the Milwaukee Brewers win the 2026 World Series?
recent.what_happened: Milwaukee swept the Dodgers 4-0 in the NLCS, which started Oct 11. They then beat the Rays in the World Series after winning Games 1 and 2 at home, 3-2 and 5-4, and the market resolved YES. My searches only confirmed the 2-0 lead, so the final series score is unverified here; the YES outcome comes from the brief.
recent.what_we_missed: The research was almost entirely about the Rays' ALCS path, which suggests it was reused from a Rays question. It left out the result of NLCS Game 1, played Oct 11 just before judgment, and anything on the Brewers' own strength, such as the NL's best record and home-field advantage. That probably explains why the forecasts (0.17–0.19) came in below the market's 0.272 with no reason given.
recent.lesson: Before you price a team's title chances, research that team's own series state, including any game that finished just before judgment; don't rely on facts gathered for its likely opponent, and don't go under the market without a specific reason.

suggested_change.change: Require at least one fact about the team named in the question and the current score of its own playoff series, and flag fact sets that only cover a different team.

recent.question: Will Likud win the most seats in the 2026 Israeli legislative election?
recent.what_happened: Likud, running on a joint list with New Hope, came first by a clear margin. The i24NEWS exit poll had Likud at 27 seats and Yashar at 20, and partial counts showed Likud at about 23% of the vote against Yashar's 16%. Results were not yet certified when this was checked, but every report had Likud well ahead. Turnout was reported as possibly the highest on record.
recent.what_we_missed: The research split the polls evenly, six leads each, and leaned toward the mainstream pollsters (Kantar, Midgam, Maariv, Kan, Channel 13), which all had Yashar ahead. It did not check how those pollsters had done before. Mainstream Israeli polls have tended to underestimate Likud in past elections, including 2015 and 2022, and this time the Channel 14 and Direct Polls numbers were closer to the result.
recent.lesson: When pollsters in a country split along house lines, look at how each group has erred in past elections before treating them as equal, and don't let a pollster's reputation outweigh a pattern of misses that consistently favor one side.

suggested_change.change: For election markets, have the research desk record each major pollster's past error for the leading parties, for example the final poll against the actual seat count in the last two or three elections, so polls can be adjusted for house effects.

recent_wins.question: Will KT Rolster win the Demacia Cup Global Invitational 2026?
recent_wins.what_happened: BNK FEARX won the Demacia Cup Global Invitational 2026, beating Team WE 3-1 in the October 17 Grand Final in Beijing. According to the reporting, FEARX also knocked KT Rolster out 3-1 in the semifinal, so the market resolved NO for KT.
recent_wins.what_worked: The forecaster's 21% came from the tournament's structure. KT still had to win three best-of-five series in a row against peers of similar strength, including FEARX, Team WE and JDG. Even a 70-75% favorite in each series wins all three only about 35-42% of the time. KT was a 5th-place LCK team that had missed Worlds, so it hardly deserved even that. The market's 46.5% looked inflated by KT's 2025 Worlds runner-up name and its 2-0 Swiss start.
recent_wins.lesson: When a market prices one team near 50% to win a multi-round single-elimination bracket, multiply out its per-series win chances. Discount brand-name reputation from past seasons in favor of current-season form, especially when peers with similar results, like FEARX, are also 2-0.

suggested_change.change: For bracket tournaments, add a step that computes the title probability by chaining estimated per-series win rates through the remaining rounds, and compares that to the market price before finalizing.

recent_wins.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $110 in October?
recent_wins.what_happened: WTI's Active Month never reached $110 in October 2026, so the market resolved No. One aggregator page was garbled: it listed $105 as a winning outcome while showing $100 and $95 as No, which doesn't add up, so I'm not relying on it. No source I found shows WTI anywhere near $110 in October, and early-October levels were about $87–91.
recent_wins.what_worked: The research found that WTI had fallen to about $87–89 by October 6, that Middle East exports were back above pre-war levels, that the G7 planned a 100M-barrel reserve release, and that US-Iran talks were underway. Together these put $110 roughly 25% above spot, and they pulled the forecast down from 0.27 without research to 0.19. Still, 0.19 was more than twice the market's 0.085, so the market was better calibrated. The forecast leaned the right way but was too high.
recent_wins.lesson: When spot sits more than 20% below a touch threshold and the news flow is de-escalating, start from the distance and the realized volatility (a 25% rally in about 3.5 weeks is roughly a 1-in-10 event even in a volatile war market), not from past peaks like the $110.93 intraday high.

suggested_change.change: For price-touch questions, have the research step compute the move needed and an implied-volatility hit probability for the remaining days, and use that number to keep tail scenarios from pushing the forecast well above a market that already prices the gap correctly.

recent_wins.question: Will the Rhine River return to normal levels between October 1 and October 31, 2026?
recent_wins.what_happened: Kaub sat near record lows for most of October: -6 cm at the start, about 11 cm around Oct 18, then 27 cm on Oct 25. Storm rain in late October gave a forecast peak of only about 66 cm around Oct 28, with levels expected to fall afterward. As reported, Kaub never reached 77 cm before November 1, so the market resolved No.
recent_wins.what_worked: The research showed how far the river had to climb: from about 0–9 cm it needed roughly 70 cm in October. It also found forecasts of a dry first half of October with only showery rain after that, and the 2018 case, where a deep low did not recover in October. The market at 52.5% and the no-research forecast at 44% ignored that gap. The margin was thinner than 19% implies, though: a late storm took the gauge to within about 11 cm of the mark, so some luck was involved.
recent_wins.lesson: For low-water recovery questions, work out how many centimetres the gauge must rise and compare that with weather-model rainfall over the catchment, instead of anchoring on how the river 'normally' behaves in that month.

suggested_change.change: Pull the official BfG/WSV multi-day Kaub forecasts and catchment rainfall totals, and size the required rise against past rain-driven rises, because a single storm here came within about 11 cm of resolving YES.

recent_wins.question: Will Likud win 30-34 seats in the 2026 Israeli legislative election?
recent_wins.what_happened: Israel voted on October 27, 2026. Likud came first, but reported counts put it at about 27 seats, below the 30–34 bracket, so the market resolved NO. Netanyahu's bloc won about 53 seats, the opposition about 48, and the Arab parties a record 19. A Wikipedia infobox still shows 32 for Likud, but that looks out of date; I did not check the Election Committee's final official figures myself.
recent_wins.what_worked: The forecaster put YES at 0.36, under 50%, so it leaned the right way. But the market was at 0.12, and that was the better price: most TV polls had Likud well under 30 seats (around 19–25), and only Channel 14 had it at 30. With no research facts, the forecaster's own estimate was about three times too high. This counts as a win only because it leaned NO, not because it beat the market.
recent_wins.lesson: For a seat-range question, collect the latest published seat projections, put them together, and work out how likely the bracket is from those numbers. Don't move toward a historical anchor like Likud's usual 30–36 seats when current polls say otherwise, and treat a polling outlier like Channel 14 as an outlier.

suggested_change.change: Before any forecast on Israeli seat brackets, require the run to pull the latest polls from several outlets (e.g., Wikipedia's polling page, Channel 12/13/Kan) and quote their average and spread, and don't let it produce a probability for an election market from zero gathered facts.

recent_wins.question: Will Anthropic have the best AI model at the end of October 2026?
recent_wins.what_happened: Anthropic did not hold #1. On the Arena Text leaderboard with style control off, Google's Gemini 4 Argon was reported at #1 around 1525–1532 in October 2026 updates, with several Anthropic models behind it at about 1501–1505. The question resolved NO, though I couldn't open the live arena.ai board and one aggregator (Swfte) still listed Claude Mythos 5 first.
recent_wins.what_worked: Very little on the forecaster's side. It put Anthropic at 0.38, above the market's 0.305, so it leaned toward the wrong answer. The money came from the 'favorites' strategy, which bet with the market favorite (Google / NO). That bet followed the board, where Gemini 4 Argon had held a lead of 20+ points since early October, and did not come from any edge in the forecast.

rules.rule: Read crypto rules for the exact strike, venue/pair and test (any touch or a close at a set candle); if mid-window, first check the venue's candles or dated reports for whether the strike was already hit and by how much, then record a venue spot timestamped under an hour old.

For crypto threshold questions, report percent distance to strike, hours left, how many of the last 14 days the venue traded through that level, realized volatility, any weekend, and timestamped same-day catalysts (yields, dollar, ETF flows, jobs data) or state none found.

For match questions, report both sides' dated absences and returns from the latest press conferences, the stand-in and the absent player's actual recent output, settled from confirmed lineups; label all-time series and head-to-heads under about 10 games as weak.

For team win or spread questions, report the home side's home-only and the visitor's road-only records, goals or points allowed over the last 5, the last 8–10 meetings, schedule strength behind any record or margin (e.g. FCS foes, first FBS year), and whether a draw resolves No.

If any game, match or stage began before the judgment time, first get its live or final score from a tracker timestamped within the hour (league site, Liquipedia), dropping undated snippets; for series add wins each side needs, venues and the cited comeback rate.

For game-total questions (goals or points), report both teams' recent game totals with dates, label a 3–4 game streak as a small sample, note weakened opponents in any blowout, and report each side's starting QB or key starter changes and defensive ranking.

For tennis completion questions, read which endings count, report the tour level's normal-finish share and each player's recent full matches, weigh only past-week injury or withdrawal news, and after start time check Tennis Explorer or ITF for w/o or ret. first.

For NFL player props, research the named player, never team D/ST rates: for TDs, his TDs per game this and last season, red-zone carries or targets and target share; for yardage, attempts per game and games past the line; plus the opponent's rank and injured defenders.

For single MMA fights, report each fighter's age, recent opponents and how those fights ended, and dated weigh-in or weight-cut news; label win streaks and common-opponent comparisons as weak evidence.

For single MLB games, report confirmed starters' ERA, ERA+ and recent starts, each bullpen's unavailable arms (injury, leave, short rest), season and road records, and form since Sept 1; label old-roster franchise streaks and series-level rates as not single-game evidence.

For video view questions, check the channel's uploads since the question opened and report any new video's upload time, hours elapsed, views and climb rate first; build references only from first-168-hour counts of recent comparable uploads, not lifetime or undated totals.

For live-streamed challenge questions near the deadline, get the current attempt's status from the past 12 hours (stream VODs, streamers' socials, fan trackers): milestones reached, gear, deaths or resets, plus the participants' own past completions and times.

For Rotten Tomatoes score questions, read the year-specific film page named in the rules, record the score, review count and dated earlier readings showing drift, and count how many negative reviews would move it past the strike before the check time.

For reality-show elimination questions, confirm every fact names the asked contestant and their own pro partner, and report couples left, eliminations per episode, live shows in the window, and every couple's judges' scores and bottom-three history.

For voted awards, check the ceremony date and search for coverage dated after it; otherwise read the official shortlist, list each finalist's dated season honours, trophies and stats, note past winners missing from it, and cite major outlets' dated rankings.

For earnings-beat questions, copy the EPS basis (GAAP diluted or adjusted) and strike from the rules, report the dated consensus and recent revisions, the last 4–8 quarters' actual-versus-consensus surprise percentages, and management's dated guidance or segment commentary.

For CPI questions, get the dated consensus and Cleveland Fed nowcast, rebuild the 12-month rate from NSA index levels incl. the month dropping out, find the monthly change the strike needs, and estimate it bottom-up: gas weight × AAA/EIA change plus typical core and food.

For GDP questions, confirm the rules' threshold and measure (BEA advance estimate, annualized real growth) match the question title, then report the release date, the latest dated GDPNow and NY Fed nowcasts, each one's typical error, and recent quarters' nowcast misses.

For Fed rate questions, take the current target range and date of the last move from the latest FOMC statement, check the strike against the upper bound under the rules' exact wording (above vs at), and report dated Fed speakers' guidance, dissents and Reuters economist polls.

For point-release (X.1) model questions, report the parent model's official launch date and current rollout stage, the company's past gaps between flagship and point releases, and any dated official announcement or release notes naming the version.
